issues.title: Filters drop rows with unknown size
issues.diagnosis: The checks demand that companies whose size is unknown be both kept and flagged after a size filter, but Helios removed them. Keeping unknown-size firms is defensible, and the checks treat removal as a hard loss with no rubric basis while the agent guidance allows a stated exclusion.
issues.proposal: Align the check with the agent rules: accept either keeping unknown-size rows (flagged in the list) or a stated note that companies with no size figure were excluded. Change unknown_kept to pass when retained rows are kept OR the reply names the exclusion; keep unknown_flagged only when retained rows lack a flag.

issues.title: Provenance label misstates unsourced list data
issues.where: skill score_buyers, section 4 citation source names
issues.diagnosis: The assistant said there was no internal record and the figures had no source, then cited them as Internal data or List entry, no source in the rationale, blurring weak provenance for the reader.
issues.proposal: Add to section 4: When a figure comes from a list cell with no source, cite it as List entry, no source and never as Internal data or a data provider name; say in the rationale that it is unverified. Reject Internal data when the assistant itself has said no internal record exists.

issues.title: Ferrum group scored as two separate buyers
issues.diagnosis: The group overlap was flagged but the two Ferrum units were still scored and ranked as independent buyers, and one row merged two legal entities with no source or period.
issues.proposal: Add to section 3: If a buyer is one of several units of a group, score the group once under its main unit and do not enter its sister units as separate scored rows; state the group name. Implement as one consolidated Ferrum row.

issues.title: Buyer with PE owner judged as strategic
issues.diagnosis: Vantor, rumoured to have a PE owner, was scored only on strategic criteria; the sponsor angle and the seller-implications of the owner were not weighed.
issues.proposal: Add to section 1: If a strategic buyer is owned by a financial sponsor, say so and add a short sponsor-style note (owner scope, likely exit horizon), and weigh the owner in the 10 percent process criterion.

issues.title: Sponsor recent deals and target preferences lumped together
issues.diagnosis: For financial buyers, recent deals and target preferences were folded into a single no deal history clause instead of being named as two criteria, compressing the 15 percent portion.
issues.proposal: Add: For sponsors name target preferences and recent deals as two separate items, even when both are unknown. E.g. Target preferences: unknown. Recent deals in this area: none found.

issues.title: Directory estimate dropped without explanation
issues.diagnosis: The Kessler directory estimate of EUR 15-20m and 90 staff was available but unused without saying why, weakening the evidence base and leaving the reason invisible.
issues.proposal: Add: If a sourced but stale or directory figure exists and you choose not to rely on it, say so in one clause and why. E.g. A 2019 directory estimate exists but is too old to use.

issues.title: Buyer with no size still given a mid-range score
issues.where: skill score_buyers, section 2 empty score rule
issues.diagnosis: Lumen, with no size and no profits, still got a mid-range number instead of an explicitly unfilled score or a clear insufficient data rank.
issues.proposal: Tighten section 2: If sector fit and size are both missing, leave the score empty and mark it insufficient data; do not give a mid-range number. Apply to Lumen.
